views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the September 24 counter-tariffs in place and do not add a new tariff or qualitative wave. Reopen the Liu He channel and offer talks aimed at freezing the scheduled January 1, 2019 lift of List 3 from 10% to 25%, without repeating the May purchase-only package that Washington discarded. Use the interval to cushion export hubs and the yuan, and treat Made in China 2025 / core IP rules as non-bargainable in any first-round offer.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. Combined U.S. Section 301 coverage is now about $250B of Chinese goods after List 3 took effect at 10% on 2018-09-24, with an announced step-up to 25% on 2019-01-01; Lists 1–2 already hit aerospace, ICT, robotics and other MIC2025-adjacent lines at 25%. That maps to the +0.5 CHN anchor (major export sectors hit, FX pressure, firm-level tech targeting) but not +1.0: merchandise exports were still ~$212B in the latest month, industrial production was still expanding (~5.9% y/y), and reserves remained above $3.07T. The pressure is real and rising: USD/CNY moved from ~6.32 in late April to 6.9263 on 2018-10-17 (~9.7% yuan depreciation toward 7); reserves fell ~$56B over the window; PBOC delivered a fourth 2018 RRR cut around 7–8 October and Shanghai still sold off; Pence’s 4 October Hudson speech recast the dispute as strategic competition and explicitly reserved tariffs on substantially more than another $250B. ZTE’s April denial order and parallel Huawei scrutiny show the U.S. can threaten national champions independently of tariffs. Action should stay near zero because further tariff escalation has little remaining U.S. import base to tax (China already moved 5–10% onto ~$60B and has already covered most of ~$130B of annual U.S. goods) and would give Washington a pretext to execute the threatened extra ~$267B. A purchase-heavy concession already failed: the 19 May joint statement (China to “significantly increase” purchases; Mnuchin “on hold”) collapsed on 29 May when the White House proceeded with 301. Rolling back first, after Pence’s speech and with no matching U.S. pause, would look like capitulation on industrial policy. Negotiate without new commitments: hold the existing retaliatory line, test whether Washington will trade a January-rate freeze for talks, and avoid a midterm-window move that the U.S. is already framing as election interference.
key_factors: US Section 301 now covers ~$250B; List 3 is 10% with a live 25% hike on 2019-01-01
China has already matched $50B and added 5–10% on ~$60B; remaining U.S. goods to tax are thin versus Trump’s extra ~$267B threat
Yuan ~6.93, reserves down ~$56B, fourth RRR cut, equity bear market — financial-stability pressure without a growth collapse
Pence 4 Oct speech plus ZTE/Huawei/MIC2025 targeting: dispute is strategic/tech, not just a goods deficit
May purchase-only truce collapsed within 10 days; repeating concede_purchases without a U.S. tariff pause would buy nothing

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5–10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
Trump directs USTR to finalize List 3: 10% tariffs on ~$200B of Chinese imports effective Sept 24, scheduled to rise to 25% on Jan 1, 2019.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
CNY per USD 6.3158 on 2018-04-23 to 6.9263 on 2018-10-17 (+9.7% yuan depreciation).
China reserves excl. gold fell from ~$3.129T (May) to ~$3.072T (Oct), about -$56B / -1.8%.
China industrial production still expanding but slowing: 106.8 (May) to 105.9 (Oct) on same-period-previous-year index.
China SA merchandise exports still ~$212B in the latest month; no collapse in headline export value.

Pence (4 Oct 2018): tariffs on $250B, highest rates on advanced industries Beijing seeks to capture; threat of substantially more than doubling unless a fair deal; China’s largest exchange down 25% in first 9 months.
Pence speech plus Bloomberg supply-chain-hack report recast the clash as long-term strategic/tech rivalry, not a contained tariff spat.
China: fight and talk; Liu He Washington visit knocked off by the $200B list; Deutsche Bank ~0.5pp growth hit, US only 12% of China exports; Trump threat of another $267B if Beijing retaliates.
Fourth 2018 RRR cut to free ~750bn yuan as US tariffs cover >$250B; yuan down ~6% YTD; easing risks more depreciation versus a hiking Fed.
